newsitem.title: UK: ISO inclined to lower Thai sugar, Cuba unchanged.
newsitem.headline: ISO inclined to lower Thai sugar, Cuba unchanged.

text.p: The International Sugar Organization said on Friday it may cut its estimate for Thai output but inclined to keep its Cuba figure unchanged in its next quarterly report at least pending more news on weather damage.

Despite factors delaying the impact of surpluses on the world market, the ISO anticipated further downward pressure on prices of raws and whites. It kept its forecast for New York raws at close to the long-term average of 10 cents a lb.
In a monthly report, the ISO said floods in cane growing areas of Thailand could delay crushing and lower sugar content.
Farmers in many areas were optimistic that the effect would be minimal.

But the Thai delegate to last month's ISO meeting had estimated output at 6.3 million tonnes tel quel "which could be interpreted as a 200,000 tonne decrease of our initial estimate for Thailand of 6.825 million tonnes, raw value", the ISO said.
It was likely to keep its Cuban estimate at 5.1 million tonnes raw value until more information was available on the damage caused by last month's Hurricane Lili.
The output for Ukraine at 3.15 million tonnes raw also did not require a major correction.
Russia was unlikely to import from the world market at the prevailing wholesale price of $450.00 a tonne despite lower sugar output expected this year.
In its latest quarterly report, the ISO has estimated Russian import demand at 3.0 million tonnes, including deliveries from the Ukraine and Cuba.

Indian production was difficult to gauge but even if production fell in 1996/97, some eight million tonnes of stocks would enable the country to maintain exports at around one million tonnes in the coming two to three seasons.
